from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Light travels at speed v1 here and v2 there.",
            "Imagine a lifeguard reaching a swimmer in the ocean.",
            "Running is faster than swimming, so paths aren't straight.",
            "Light also takes a path to minimize travel time."
        ]

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        self.place_in_area(water_rect, "D3", "E5")
        
        # Broken Pencil

        self.play(Create(glass_outline), FadeIn(water_rect))
        self.play(Create(pencil_top), Create(pencil_bottom))

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(glass_outline), FadeOut(water_rect), FadeOut(pencil_top), FadeOut(pencil_bottom))
        
        # Interface Line
        interface_y = (self.grid["C3"][1] + self.grid["D3"][1]) / 2
        interface_line = Line(start=[0, interface_y, 0], end=[6, interface_y, 0], color=WHITE)
        
        # Sand and Water Regions
        sand_bg = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#EDC9AF", fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(sand_bg, "A1", "C6")
        sand_bg.shift(UP * 0.15) # Adjust to align with interface_y
        
        water_bg = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water_bg, "D1", "F6")
        water_bg.shift(DOWN * 0.15)
        
        self.play(Create(interface_line), FadeIn(sand_bg), FadeIn(water_bg))
        
        v1_label = Text("v₁", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, "B2")
        v2_label = Text("v₂", color="#FF0000").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, "E2")
        
        self.play(Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        pointA = Dot(self.grid["B1"], color=WHITE)
        labelA = Text("Lifeguard (A)", font_size=16).next_to(pointA, UP)
        pointB = Dot(self.grid["E6"], color=WHITE)
        labelB = Text("Swimmer (B)", font_size=16).next_to(pointB, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(pointA), Write(labelA), Create(pointB), Write(labelB))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Dashed Straight Line
        straight_path = DashedLine(pointA.get_center(), pointB.get_center(), color=GRAY)
        self.play(Create(straight_path))
        
        # Traveling Dot
        traveler = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        
        # Calculate intersection with interface for timing mathematically
        # instead of point_from_proportion which fails on DashedLine
        intersection_point = (pointA.get_center() + pointB.get_center()) / 2
        
        # Animation
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(traveler, Line(pointA.get_center(), intersection_point)), run_time=1, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(traveler, Line(intersection_point, pointB.get_center())), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(FadeOut(traveler))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Normal line
        optimal_x_pos = intersection_point + RIGHT * 1.0
        normal_line = DashedLine(optimal_x_pos + UP*1.5, optimal_x_pos + DOWN*1.5, color="#808080")
        
        path_segments = VGroup(
            Line(pointA.get_center(), optimal_x_pos, color=WHITE),
            Line(optimal_x_pos, pointB.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        )
        
        angle1 = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=PI/2, angle=-PI/4, arc_center=optimal_x_pos)
        theta1 = Text("θ₁", font_size=20).next_to(angle1, UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        angle2 = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=-PI/2, angle=PI/6, arc_center=optimal_x_pos)
        theta2 = Text("θ₂", font_size=20).next_to(angle2, DOWN+LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        v1_vec = Arrow(start=pointA.get_center(), end=pointA.get_center() + RIGHT*0.8, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        v2_vec = Arrow(start=pointB.get_center(), end=pointB.get_center() + RIGHT*0.4, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        
        self.play(Create(normal_line), Create(path_segments))
        self.play(Create(angle1), Write(theta1), Create(angle2), Write(theta2))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v1_vec), GrowArrow(v2_vec))
        
        pointX = Dot(optimal_x_pos, color=WHITE)
        self.add(pointX)
        
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(optimal_x_pos[0])
        
        def update_path(path):
            curr_x = x_tracker.get_value()
            new_p = np.array([curr_x, interface_y, 0])
            path[0].set_points_as_corners([pointA.get_center(), new_p])
            path[1].set_points_as_corners([new_p, pointB.get_center()])
            pointX.move_to(new_p)

        path_segments.add_updater(update_path)
        
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(optimal_x_pos[0] - 1.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(optimal_x_pos[0] + 0.5), run_time=1)
        path_segments.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Let’s map the journey from point A to B.",
            "- Light crosses the interface at a variable point x.",

            "- Pythagoras gives the length of each path segment.",

        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout("Setting the Geometric Stage", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors for consistency
        C1 = YELLOW
        C2 = BLUE
        C3 = GREEN
        C4 = RED
        C5 = PURPLE_A

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(C1))
        
        interface = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        
        dot_a = Dot(self.grid["B2"], color=C1)
        label_a = Text("A", color=C1, font_size=24).next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(self.grid["E5"], color=C1)
        label_b = Text("B", color=C1, font_size=24).next_to(dot_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(interface))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a, label_a), FadeIn(dot_b, label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(C2))
        
        dot_x = Dot(self.grid["D4"], color=C2)
        label_x = Text("x", color=C2, font_size=24).next_to(dot_x, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_x, label_x))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(C3))
        
        dash_a = DashedLine(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D2"], color=C3)
        dash_b = DashedLine(self.grid["E5"], self.grid["D5"], color=C3)
        label_a_val = Text("a", color=C3, font_size=24).next_to(dash_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_b_val = Text("b", color=C3, font_size=24).next_to(dash_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        arrow_l = DoubleArrow(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D5"], buff=0, color=C3, tip_length=0.1)
        arrow_l.shift(UP * 0.4)
        label_l = Text("L", color=C3, font_size=24).next_to(arrow_l, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        brace_x = BraceBetweenPoints(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D4"], direction=UP, color=C2, buff=0.1)
        label_x_seg = Text("x", color=C2, font_size=24).next_to(brace_x, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        brace_lx = BraceBetweenPoints(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["D5"], direction=UP, color=C2, buff=0.1)
        label_lx_seg = Text("L-x", color=C2, font_size=24).next_to(brace_lx, UP, buff=0.05)
        
        self.play(Create(dash_a), Create(dash_b), FadeIn(label_a_val, label_b_val))
        self.play(Create(arrow_l), FadeIn(label_l))
        self.play(Create(brace_x), FadeIn(label_x_seg), Create(brace_lx), FadeIn(label_lx_seg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Using Text with Unicode instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX FileNotFoundError
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(C4))
        
        path1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D4"], color=C4)
        path2 = Line(self.grid["D4"], self.grid["E5"], color=C4)
        
        formula_d1 = Text("d₁ = √(a² + x²)", color=C4, font_size=24)
        formula_d2 = Text("d₂ = √(b² + (L-x)²)", color=C4, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(formula_d1, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_d2, "F2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(path1), Create(path2))
        self.play(Write(formula_d1), Write(formula_d2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Using Text with Unicode for total travel time
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(C5))
        
        time_total = Text("T = d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂", color=C5, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(time_total, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(time_total))
        self.wait(2)

        self.place_at_grid(snells_law, "E3")
        
        self.play(Write(snells_law))
        self.play(Indicate(snells_law))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Application: From Eyes to Fiber Optics"
        lines = [
            "This simple law governs how lenses focus light.",
            "It also explains how fiber optics carry internet signals.",
            "Light's logic of least time shapes our modern world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)

        # Draw Lens
        # Approximate a convex lens using two arcs
        lens_color = "#FFFFFF"
        ray_color = "#FFFF00"
        
        lens_left = ArcBetweenPoints(
            start=self.grid['A3'] + DOWN*0.2, 
            end=self.grid['C3'] + UP*0.2, 
            angle=-TAU/8, 
            color=lens_color
        )
        lens_right = ArcBetweenPoints(
            start=self.grid['C3'] + UP*0.2, 
            end=self.grid['A3'] + DOWN*0.2, 
            angle=-TAU/8, 
            color=lens_color
        )
        lens = VGroup(lens_left, lens_right)
        
        # Rays
        focus_point = self.grid['B6']
        
        # Ray 1: Top
        ray1_in = Line(self.grid['A1'], self.grid['A3'], color=ray_color)
        ray1_out = Line(self.grid['A3'], focus_point, color=ray_color)
        
        # Ray 2: Middle
        ray2_in = Line(self.grid['B1'], self.grid['B3'], color=ray_color)
        ray2_out = Line(self.grid['B3'], focus_point, color=ray_color)
        
        # Ray 3: Bottom
        ray3_in = Line(self.grid['C1'], self.grid['C3'], color=ray_color)
        ray3_out = Line(self.grid['C3'], focus_point, color=ray_color)
        
        rays = VGroup(ray1_in, ray2_in, ray3_in, ray1_out, ray2_out, ray3_out)

        self.play(Create(lens))
        self.play(
            Create(ray1_in), Create(ray2_in), Create(ray3_in),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Create(ray1_out), Create(ray2_out), Create(ray3_out),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Clear previous visuals and highlight second line
        self.play(
            FadeOut(lens), FadeOut(rays),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Draw Fiber Core (parallel lines)
        core_top = Line(self.grid['D1'], self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE)
        core_bottom = Line(self.grid['E1'], self.grid['E6'], color=WHITE)
        fiber_core = VGroup(core_top, core_bottom)
        
        # Fiber Ray - Bouncing via Total Internal Reflection
        # Calculate points for a zigzag path
        p1 = self.grid['D1'] + DOWN*0.5  # Entry point (midpoint D-E)
        p2 = self.grid['D2']             # Hit top
        p3 = self.grid['E3']             # Hit bottom
        p4 = self.grid['D4']             # Hit top
        p5 = self.grid['E5']             # Hit bottom
        p6 = self.grid['D6'] + DOWN*0.5  # Exit point
        
        fiber_ray_path = VMobject(color=ray_color)
        fiber_ray_path.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6])
        
        self.play(Create(fiber_core))
        self.play(Create(fiber_ray_path), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Clear fiber and highlight third line
        self.play(
            FadeOut(fiber_core), FadeOut(fiber_ray_path),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        closing_text = Text("Snell's Law: The Logic of Light", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(closing_text, 'B2', 'D5')
        
        self.play(Write(closing_text))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Logic of Light: Proving Snell's Law via Fermat's Principle
outline.target_audience: Advanced high school students or first-year university physics students

sections.title: The Refraction Mystery
sections.content: Introduce the phenomenon of refraction using a visual mystery. Define the basic parameters: incident angle (θ1), refracted angle (θ2), and the change in speed between two media (v1 and v2). Pose the question: Why does light choose this specific path?
sections.example: A visual of a 'broken' pencil in a glass of water, transitioning to an animation of a lifeguard (Leo) on a beach needing to reach a swimmer in the ocean. Leo runs faster on sand than he swims in water, so he shouldn't take a straight line, but a path that minimizes total time.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat's Principle of Least Time
sections.content: Explain the foundational principle: Light travels between two points along the path that requires the least amount of time. Define the Refractive Index (n = c/v) to link speed and material properties.
sections.example: An animation showing three potential paths for a light beam: one straight, one overly angled, and the 'optimal' path glowing brightly to illustrate 'Least Time'.

sections.title: Setting the Geometric Stage
sections.content: Establish a coordinate system. Point A is in Medium 1 (speed v1), Point B is in Medium 2 (speed v2). Let the horizontal distance be 'L' and the vertical distances be 'a' and 'b'. Let 'x' be the variable point on the interface where light crosses.
sections.example: A clear geometric diagram showing a right-angled triangle in the top medium (hypotenuse L1 = sqrt(a² + x²)) and another in the bottom medium (hypotenuse L2 = sqrt(b² + (L-x)²)).

sections.title: The Mathematical Derivation
sections.content: Construct the Time Function: T(x) = (L1/v1) + (L2/v2). To find the minimum time, we take the derivative with respect to x and set it to zero [dT/dx = 0]. Show how the chain rule transforms the algebraic lengths into trigonometric ratios.
sections.example: Animated math overlay: Showing d/dx [sqrt(a² + x²) / v1] becoming (x / (v1 * L1)). Graphically highlight that x/L1 is exactly sin(θ1) and (L-x)/L2 is sin(θ2).

sections.title: The Grand Reveal: Snell’s Law
sections.content: Simplify the result of the derivation: sin(θ1)/v1 = sin(θ2)/v2. Multiply both sides by 'c' (speed of light in vacuum) to introduce the refractive indices (n1 and n2), resulting in the final form: n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2).
sections.example: The equation n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2) pulses in gold light on the screen. A side-by-side comparison shows that if n2 > n1 (like air to glass), the light must bend toward the normal to 'save time'.

sections.title: Application: From Eyes to Fiber Optics
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate how this law governs modern technology and biology. Mention how lenses focus light and how Total Internal Reflection (a consequence of Snell's Law) works.
sections.example: A cross-section of a fiber optic cable showing a light signal 'bouncing' inside because the angle is too steep to escape, allowing high-speed internet to reach our homes.

storyboard.title: The Refraction Mystery
lecture_lines: Why does light bend when moving between different materials?
Light travels at speed v1 here and v2 there.
Imagine a lifeguard reaching a swimmer in the ocean.
Running is faster than swimming, so paths aren't straight.
Light also takes a path to minimize travel time.
animations: Create a Glass (unfilled Rectangle, white #FFFFFF) with a blue Water level (Rectangle #1E90FF). Add a slanted Line (#D4AF37) that breaks/offsets at the water line.
Transition: Remove glass. Create a horizontal Interface Line (#FFFFFF). Top region colored #EDC9AF (sand), bottom #1E90FF (water). Points A (top-left) and B (bottom-right).

Show two vectors at Point A and Point B representing speeds v1 (#00FF00) and v2 (#FF0000).
Draw a solid path from A to a point X on the interface, then to B. Show the point X shifting to minimize time. Add Normal Line (dashed #808080) and arcs for θ1, θ2.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Fermat's Principle of Least Time
lecture_lines: Fermat’s Principle states light takes the quickest path.
Index n equals vacuum speed c divided by material speed.
Light optimizes its journey between any two points.
animations: Show a point A and point B. Draw a straight yellow line (#FFFF00) between them.
Introduce a horizontal boundary. Show three paths from A to B: one straight, one bending early, one bending late.
Fade out non-optimal paths. Highlight the 'least time' path in Gold (#FFD700). Display text 'n = c/v' (#FFFFFF) in the corner.

storyboard.title: Setting the Geometric Stage
lecture_lines: Let’s map the journey from point A to B.
Light crosses the interface at a variable point x.
Distances depend on heights a, b and width L.
Pythagoras gives the length of each path segment.
These segments relate to travel times T1 and T2.
animations: Draw a horizontal Interface Line (#FFFFFF). Mark Point A above and Point B below.
Add dashed vertical lines from A and B to the interface, labeled 'a' and 'b'. Label the total horizontal span 'L'.
Place a point 'x' on the interface. Draw lines from A to x and x to B. Label segments 'x' and 'L-x'.

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Derivation
lecture_lines: Total time T equals distance divided by speed.
To find the minimum time, set dT/dx to zero.
The derivative reveals ratios of distances and speeds.
Geometry shows these ratios are sines of the angles.
This optimization leads directly to light's final path.
animations: Display T(x) = (sqrt(a^2 + x^2) / v1) + (sqrt(b^2 + (L-x)^2) / v2). Label terms L1 and L2 (#FFFFFF).
Animate the derivative operator d/dx being applied to T(x). Set result to 0.
Show the step-by-step simplification resulting in x / (v1 * L1) = (L-x) / (v2 * L2).
Re-display the triangles from Section 3. Highlight the ratios as sin(θ1) and sin(θ2) using color pulses (#FFFF00).
Finalize the line: sin(θ1) / v1 = sin(θ2) / v2.

storyboard.title: The Grand Reveal: Snell’s Law
lecture_lines: Sin(theta 1) over v1 equals sin(theta 2) over v2.
Multiply by c to introduce refractive indices n1 and n2.
Snell’s Law: n1 sin(theta 1) equals n2 sin(theta 2).
animations: Display sin(θ1) / v1 = sin(θ2) / v2. Highlight v1 and v2.
Animate 'c' (speed of light) appearing in the numerators. Show n1 = c/v1 and n2 = c/v2 definitions.
Transition the formula to n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2). Make it glow Gold (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: Application: From Eyes to Fiber Optics
lecture_lines: This simple law governs how lenses focus light.
It also explains how fiber optics carry internet signals.
Light's logic of least time shapes our modern world.
animations: Draw a Lens shape (#FFFFFF) next to the eye icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eye.svg]. Trace multiple light rays (#FFFF00) refracting through it to a single point.
Draw a horizontal 'Fiber Core' (two parallel lines). Animate a ray (#FFFF00) bouncing inside via Total Internal Reflection.
